description: Out-of-tree explicit spec (Axiom-owned) for the relational sizing theorem over stew/base36.nim encodedLength/decodedLength. The subject tree (nim-stew v0.5.2 clone) is READ-ONLY; this file is the only legitimate place the claim may live. Loaded via explicitSpecFromOverlay, which pins origin to soExplicit and fails closed otherwise.

theorem.statement: forall n : Int, 0 <= n and n <= 33297371974204966 -> decodedLength (encodedLength n) = n (equality, exact) and encodedLength n >= 1 and not overflowAt (encodedLength n) and not overflowAt (decodedLength (encodedLength n))
theorem.boundDerivation: high(int) div 277 on a 64-bit int; exactly tight: 277*n = 9223372036854775582 <= high(int) at the bound (headroom 225), 277*(n+1) = 9223372036854775859 > high(int) overflows
theorem.character: relational theorem about the two sizing functions' relationship under the stated domain precondition

semanticCaveats: Nim int is pointer-width signed; the bound is width-derived: 64-bit = 33297371974204966, 32-bit = 7752648, 16-bit = 118. It must be re-derived per target width.
Nim div truncates toward zero; Lean Int.div floors. They coincide only for n >= 0, so 0 <= n is a discharged hypothesis, not decoration.

{.push raises: [].} does NOT track or prevent OverflowDefect (Nim's Defect family is outside the effect system): encodedLength/decodedLength can defect at runtime with no visible effect-contract trace. The certificate must say so.
certificateIdentity: target int width and (cpu, os, triple)
build/checks profile: checked Defect vs unchecked wrap are different program meanings
division semantic profile: truncation vs floor vs Nat
domain precondition as an IRFuncDef.preConditions entry (0 <= n and n <= 33297371974204966)
pinned Nim 2.2.10 (overflow-check defaults are version behavior)
note that raises: [] does not cover OverflowDefect
subject hash and IR digest of the derived IRFuncDef
nonClaims: NOT a postcondition of decodedLength alone
NOT a postcondition of encodedLength alone
NOT a buffer-safety claim about encode or decode (encode's write bound is the next slice)
NOT valid for any int width other than the one pinned in the certificate
NOT a claim that encodedLength/decodedLength cannot raise at runtime (OverflowDefect is outside the effect system)
NOT a claim that nim-stew was modified or annotated in-tree (Zero-Footprint)
